provenance.inputs: inputs.txt (excerpt L and excerpt E, preserved verbatim)
provenance.language: English, matching the language of the request; the two excerpts are quoted in their original wording
provenance.note: The counts below come from one invented teaching sentence. No case records, reporting-database query, statistical engine or literature search was involved, and no managed analysis was started, so nothing here is a drug-safety finding.

scope.data_source: one unblinded convenience cohort of 20 adults (teaching evidence E)
scope.population_in_proposed_use_elsewhere: children, addressed separately in off-label-analysis.json and not by this cohort

observed_counts.denominator_definition: the 20 participants enrolled in the single teaching cohort. Whatever it is divided by, it stays that cohort: not a treated population, not person-time, and not a count of cases from a reporting database.
observed_counts.basis: verbatim teaching evidence E; both proportions recomputed from the counts by check_evidence_framing.py (run recorded in checks-output.txt)

reasons: There is no comparator arm or reported background occurrence of rash, so the proportion observed cannot be separated from what would have occurred without the medicine.
There was no adjudication: the report does not say how rash was defined, who assessed it, or whether that assessment was blinded.
The cohort is described as unblinded, so ascertainment of both improvement and rash is open to detection bias.
Exposure information is absent: no dose, route, duration, time from exposure to event, or dechallenge and rechallenge is reported.
Concomitant medicines, comorbidities and any history of rash are not reported, so alternative explanations cannot be excluded.
Sampling was by convenience, with no consecutive or random selection described.
what_would_be_required: a comparator group or a reported background rate in a comparable population
an explicit event definition and a documented adjudication procedure
exposure timing relative to the event, with dose, route and duration
concomitant medicines and history of similar events, with dechallenge information where available

reasons: A single convenience cohort does not define the population at risk.
There is no person-time, no exposure denominator and no complete follow-up.
Participants were selected by convenience, so the cohort is not representative of adults treated with TeachingDrugA.
15.0% describes this cohort and nothing wider. Read as a rate for treated patients, or as the frequency a clinician should expect to see, it would be wrong.
population_incidence.usable_statement: In this cohort, 3 of 20 adults were reported as having rash. That is all the supplied material supports.

reporting_database_context.signal_strength: not assessable from the supplied material
reporting_database_context.disproportionality: not computed. Nothing was queried for this file, so the missing metric is a piece of evidence that is absent, not evidence of absence
reporting_database_context.stimulated_reporting_or_duplicate_report: not assessable: no reporting-database records were examined

comparative_safety.reason: No second medicine and no comparator group are supplied, so no comparative safety statement is possible.

seriousness_and_context.consequence: The event cannot be graded for seriousness from the supplied wording.

limitations: 20 participants, convenience sample, unblinded, no comparator, no adjudication.
Adults only; the cohort says nothing about children.
Counts are as reported in one sentence; no case-level detail, timing or follow-up is available.
Invented teaching material: no real drug-safety conclusion can be drawn from it.
claims_not_supported: causality between TeachingDrugA and the rash
a rash rate or expected frequency among treated patients

human_review.reason: Any use of these counts in a real safety assessment needs a source that reports design, adjudication and comparator information.
